candidate.answerReason: Sixty pills provide 120 half-pill doses. At one dose every two days, this covers about 240 days, or approximately 8 months.

methods.label: Count half-pill doses
methods.explanation:
Each whole pill provides two half-pill doses, so \(60\) pills provide
\[60\cdot2=120\text{ doses}.\]
One dose is taken every two days, so these doses cover about \(120\cdot2=240\) days. Using approximately \(30\) days per month gives
\[240\div30=8\text{ months}.\]
The supply lasts approximately \(8\) months, choice \(\mathrm D\).
methods.levelReason: Uses counting halves, whole-number quantitative relationships, and an elementary approximation of month length.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target cnm_p184 is counting fractional portions in a supply. The method realizes this by counting two halves per pill. It uses cnm_p111 for the dose-to-day relationship, with unit-fraction meaning and calendar lengths supplied by cnm_p079 and cnm_p091.
